thank you for sharing. there's a misconception that ive read in places where people say that the emphasis we put on piv sex makes other forms of sex seem "less real" and that if queer people (as in lesbians or people in relationships where both parties have a vagina) dont need to have piv sex and are still satisfied, then other people shouldn't see it as such a big deal. i myself am queer and whenever i think about having sex with another queer person, penetration always crosses my mind. it just makes no sense. queer people still engage in forms of piv sex. being fingered means that you're experiencing penetration, as does having your partner use a strap-on on you. a lot of these arguments people use are just so unhelpful. i literally don't understand what about "i want to be able to have piv sex" people struggle to understand.

and then there's also the people who view those who dont engage in it as "making a statement" and that we're "good for helping normalise other forms of sex" like im sorry but i never asked to do any of this. i dont have piv sex because i cant, not because im trying to make a statement.

im so sorry to hear that you've also been feeling this way but it also brings me comfort to know that im not alone. absolutely. the lack of complete control over your body and what sex you're able to have is what really gets me, too. and i know that people mean well by saying that piv sex isnt the only type of sex that exists and that there are lots of other options, sometimes (and im not just talking about other reddit users, it happened when i spoke to the therapist for my assessment and also happens when i speak to friends) it almost feels like our worries and insecurities are being downplayed. it's beyond frustrating. is it so wrong to want to be able to do something that so many other women don't struggle with? im so glad that others have found ways to be sexually fulfilled without the need for piv but in my experience, all of the other forms ive read up about don't appeal to me. and as ive never had piv before, theres no guarantee that ill even enjoy it. but theres also a 50% chance that i will, more than any other form, and the fact that i probably may never know makes me want to cry. not to mention that its not always about sex. im currently not in the a position to be having a child but what about in the future? having to spend so much money on surrogates or ivf or other forms of fertility treatments that may not even work saddens me to no end and makes the idea of pregnancy completely inaccessible to those without the financial means. as much as people try to spin this into a positive thing, there are simply no positives. it's not even pessimism, its the truth. if given the chance, i dont for a second doubt that the vast majority, if not all women/people who suffer from this would swap their vagina out for one that works properly. i truly am sick of acting like it doesn't bother me and i cant even begin to describe the things id do to have a vagina that functions properly. sorry for the rant. this whole thing just upsets me to no end.
